content.text:
Found it exactly. Commit `2a5df16` (Sep 14, 2016) introduced local final variables `actualNode`/`sourceNode` caching `actual.currentNode`/`source.currentNode` at the top of `reclaim()`, and replaced the live `source.currentNode.getChildren(...)` / `source.currentNode.keySequence.iterator()` calls inside the loop with the cached `sourceNode` reference. But within the loop, `source.moveDown()` mutates `source.currentNode`, so after that call the stale `sourceNode` variable no longer reflects the current node — the next iteration's `sourceNode.getChildren(...)` / `sourceNode.keySequence.iterator()` operate on the wrong (stale) node. The fix commit `04b514d` simply reverts those two usages back to the live `source.currentNode`.

Note: the actual side (`actual.currentNode`) was already using the live reference even in `2a5df16`'s version (the diff shows `actual.currentNode.getChildren(...)` unchanged), so only the source side had this latent bug — consistent with the fix only touching the `source` lines.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 2a5df16ac0d3576a62440a0da4818833df5cd8e5

## Reasoning
(1) I used `git log -L` on the `reclaim` method in `PatriciaTreeMutable.java` to trace its full history. This showed the method was originally introduced in `d9a9c29` (2014) always using live `source.currentNode` / `actual.currentNode` accessors. Then `2a5df16` (Sep 14, 2016) refactored the method to cache `actual.currentNode` and `source.currentNode` into local `final` variables `actualNode`/`sourceNode` at entry, and used those cached variables for the `getChildren`/`keySequence.iterator()` calls on the "source" side inside the traversal loop.

(2) The bug: inside the `else if (actItr.hasNext())` branch, the code calls `source.moveDown()`, which updates `source.currentNode` to point to a new/different node. However, after that `2a5df16` refactor, the subsequent line `srcItr = sourceNode.keySequence.iterator();` (and the `sourceNode.getChildren(...)` call before `moveDown()`) referenced the stale, pre-`moveDown()` cached `sourceNode` local variable instead of the live `source.currentNode`. This means subsequent loop iterations traversed children of the wrong (original) node rather than the node just moved into, breaking the reclamation logic for the source traverser.

(3) The fix commit `04b514d` changes exactly these two lines back from `sourceNode.getChildren(...)` / `sourceNode.keySequence.iterator()` to `source.currentNode.getChildren(...)` / `source.currentNode.keySequence.iterator()`, restoring live access. Notably, the corresponding "actual" side calls (`actual.currentNode.getChildren(...)`, `actual.currentNode.keySequence.iterator()`) were never changed to use the cached `actualNode` variable in `2a5df16` — only the source side was (incorrectly) switched to the cache, which is exactly the asymmetry that the fix commit corrects. This strongly indicates `2a5df16` is the commit that introduced the bug, with no intervening commits touching this logic between `2a5df16` and the fix `04b514d`.

I'm confident in this identification since the `git log -L` history shows a direct, unambiguous introduction-then-revert pattern on the exact same lines with no other commits touching this code path in between.
